chunks: And everything in this book that is narrated from Muhammad ibn Bijil, the brother of Ali ibn Bijil, has been transmitted by me from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq Al-Nahdi, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ribaat, from Muhammad ibn Bijil, the brother of Ali ibn Bijil ibn Aqil Al-Kufi.

key_terms.ابْنُ عَقِيلٍ: Ibn Aqil, indicating lineage to Aqil ibn Abi Talib
key_terms.الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.الْهَيْثَمُ بْنُ أَبِي مَسْرُوقٍ: Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a phrase of respect for the father
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a key narrator in the chain
key_terms.عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ رَبَاطٍ: Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ribaat, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ بَجِيلٍ: Muhammad ibn Bijil, a prominent narrator

ai.seo_question: Who is the narrator chain for Muhammad ibn Bijil in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage provides a crucial biographical verification (takhrij) for Muhammad ibn Bijil, a key narrator in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*, by tracing the chain back through his brother Ali ibn Bijil to establish the authenticity of the reports. It highlights the scholarly practice of distinguishing between the narrator and his relative to ensure the integrity of the isnad, reflecting the rigorous attention to detail characteristic of Shia hadith sciences.
